title: Free-fall lab
target: Estimate g from measured motion and discuss measurement limits.
criteria: Keep supplied examples separate from measurements.
Find acceleration from a velocity-time slope.
Use repeated trials and explain uncertainty.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A worksheet provides a sample velocity table. How should a student describe calculations made from it?
options: A new observation of the local gravitational field.
Their own measured trial without doing the experiment.
Exact proof that sensors have no uncertainty.
cpa.guide: Supplied data can test reasoning but do not establish personal measurement.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Which record distinguishes an actual trial from a worked example?
options: Only the expected value of g.
A claim that every number is exact.
Recorded sensor readings, units, setup, and trial identification.
cpa.guide: Traceable observations identify what was actually measured.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Take downward positive. Supplied velocity changes from 1 to 7 m/s over 0.6 s. What is acceleration?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: With upward positive, a fitted free-fall v–t line has slope −9.6 m/s². What does this mean?
options: The ball must move upward the entire time.
cpa.guide: The sign gives direction; magnitude is positive.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Supplied trials give 9.4, 9.8, and 10.2 m/s². What are the mean and full observed interval?
cpa.guide: Mean = 29.4/3 = 9.8; interval runs from minimum to maximum.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Repeated values cluster tightly but all differ from the expected g. Which next check is useful?
options: Replace observations with the expected number.
Calibration and systematic timing or length-scale errors.
Delete all readings without documenting why.
cpa.guide: Repeatability does not rule out systematic bias.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
